summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a complex medical history including fibrosing mesenteritis, chronic TPN dependence via a tunneled femoral catheter, and recurrent line infections was admitted for right-sided chest pain. Imaging revealed a subacute anterior fifth rib fracture, likely due to prolonged vomiting, and a blood culture from her femoral line grew Enterococcus avium. She was treated with intravenous daptomycin and vancomycin antibiotic locks in the catheter, with no need for line removal per Infectious Disease. Pain improved with a short course of Toradol, later discontinued due to GI concerns, and she was transitioned back to morphine. Repeat blood cultures remained negative, and she was discharged home with home health services to complete a 10-day course of daptomycin, continue TPN, and perform vancomycin locks. Follow-up was arranged with Infectious Disease and primary care.
problems: Pathologic fracture of other specified site
Other and unspecified infection due to central venous catheter
Streptococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, streptococcus, group D [Enterococcus]
